name: NOFX
label: Epitaph
lede: Three Los Angeles punks turned down every major label, kept their video off MTV, and after 41 years said goodbye over three nights at home in San Pedro.

eras.title: Negative FX, minus the hardcore
eras.text: Three Los Angeles kids borrow a name from a Boston hardcore band and play fast, jokey punk. Drummers swap, a new guitarist dies, and a tiny local label puts out the first records.

years.h: A Boston hardcore band lends NOFX its name
years.p: Mike Burkett, soon to be Fat Mike, on bass and vocals, guitarist [[Eric Melvin|25a66564-3655-44a8-86be-c60fdf447b23]] and drummer Erik Sandin start in Los Angeles, shortening Negative FX to NOFX.

years.h: Germs drummer Don Bolles produces a demo nobody hears
years.p: Thalidomide Child is the band's first recording, with [[Don Bolles|538ca22d-da9b-4b4d-ba74-4244f327c72b]] of [[The Germs|42c4b58d-2e28-41d4-bfe5-4edee68386cf]] behind the board. Fat Mike joked that no copies existed; it was reissued in 2012.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the demo "did not sell many copies."

years.h: Guitarist Dave Allen dies in a car crash, four months after joining
years.p: Dave Allen is killed in the accident, per Wikipedia. Drums are shaky too: Erik Sandin briefly leaves, and Scott Sellers and Scott Aldahl fill in.

years.h: Mystic, a small Los Angeles label, puts out the first EP
years.p: The self-titled NOFX EP is followed in 1986 by So What If We're on Mystic!

years.h: Dave Casillas makes it two guitars
years.p: Casillas gives NOFX its first two-guitar lineup. It records the debut album the following year.

eras.title: Epitaph moves in
eras.text: Brett Gurewitz of Bad Religion produces the first album, and his label Epitaph becomes NOFX's home for a decade. The guitarists change, and a trumpet player loosens the sound.

years.h: Brett Gurewitz produces Liberal Animation
years.p: NOFX's debut album first comes out on Mystic and on Fat Mike's own small Wassail label. Epitaph reissues it in 1991.
years.xp: Wikipedia says Fat Mike became a vegetarian after writing the album. The Ruthie's Inn set from June 1988, taped on VHS in Berkeley, shows the lineup that made it, with Casillas on second guitar.

years.h: S&M Airlines lands on Epitaph
years.p: Epitaph Records puts out album two, quick, melodic and wisecracking, which is the way the band stays. Steve Kidwiller takes over guitar from Dave Casillas around the same time.

years.h: Fat Mike and his wife start a label on the side
years.p: Erin Burkett and Fat Mike found Fat Wreck Chords in San Francisco. It grows into one of punk's biggest independents, home to [[Lagwagon|c7788fba-e635-4d8b-a937-01a68ab154e3]], [[Strung Out|0220a594-56a1-47ca-8288-001ead3a3546]] and [[No Use for a Name|d7bd0fad-2f06-4936-89ad-60c5b6ada3c1]].

years.cap: NOFX on stage at The Pompadour, November 1991
years.h: El Hefe arrives with a trumpet
years.p: Aaron Abeyta, known as [[El Hefe|06e0fdef-679a-403f-a8a7-f6bf2523959d]], joins on lead guitar and trumpet for Ribbed, and Kidwiller leaves. Hefe stays for the rest of the band's life.

eras.title: No thanks to the majors
eras.text: NOFX sells records by the thousand with no major label and no MTV. The liner notes tell the majors to leave them alone, and the band does it its own way.

years.h: The members' backgrounds become an album title
years.p: White Trash, Two Heebs and a Bean describes the band, and it's the first full album after El Hefe joined.

years.h: Punk in Drublic takes six years to go gold
years.p: Recorded at Westbeach Recorders in Hollywood with Ryan Greene, 39 minutes including "Linoleum", "The Brews" and "Leave It Alone".
years.xp:
The title is a spoonerism of "Drunk in Public". It peaked at number 12 on Billboard's Heatseekers chart and, six years after release, became NOFX's only RIAA gold record, per Wikipedia. A hidden bit at the end has El Hefe doing cartoon voices.

"Jeff Wears Birkenstocks" was written about an Epitaph employee, and Birkenstock made a short documentary about it in 2017.

years.h: The "Leave It Alone" video never goes to MTV
years.p: KROQ plays the song, but the band makes the video and keeps it away from the channel.
years.xp: Fat Mike's reason, per Wikipedia: "we just didn't want to be a part of that machine."

years.big: "We've been doing fine all these years without you so leave us alone!"
years.h: NOFX answers the majors on the back of a live album
years.p: The note ships with I Heard They Suck Live!!, and the band stays independent.
years.xp: The line is printed in the 1995 liner notes, per Wikipedia.

years.cap: Ticket stub for the Warped Tour, August 4, 1996, with NOFX on the bill
years.h: Germany bans the cover of Eating Lamb
years.p: The vinyl edition of Heavy Petting Zoo is retitled Eating Lamb and pulled from sale over its cover art. The record is also NOFX's first on the Billboard chart, at number 63.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the Eating Lamb version "was banned from sale in Germany" for its obscene cover.

years.h: The Decline is one song, and it runs 18 minutes
years.p: A single-track EP of political commentary, among the longest punk songs ever released.
years.xp: Wikipedia calls it "fiery and cynical social commentary." NOFX plays it at the 2024 farewell shows.

eras.title: Politics, and a label run by the bassist
eras.text: After Epitaph, NOFX records for the label Fat Mike runs. Politics takes over the band's public life, along with a subscription vinyl club and a TV tour diary.

years.h: Epitaph gets one more record, Pump Up the Valuum
years.p: NOFX's eighth album, out in 2000, ends the Epitaph run. After it the band works with Fat Wreck Chords, the label Fat Mike runs.

years.big: "We raised over a $1 million for John Kerry"
years.h: The War on Errorism goes after George W. Bush
years.p: Fat Mike's count, in Spin, of the Rock Against Bush campaign. He also ran punkvoter.com and compiled two Rock Against Bush albums.
years.xp: Fat Mike told Spin he was at the Democratic Convention, rubbing elbows with Larry David and Michael Moore. Then Bush won in 2004, and it hit him hard. Eric Melvin pointed to that loss as a possible breaking point for the band.

years.h: Wolves in Wolves' Clothing follows a year of monthly EPs
years.p: The 7-Inch of the Month Club ran 12 releases from February 2005 to March 2006, with fans submitting cover art for the EPs.

years.cap: NOFX on stage at Warped Tour, Uniondale, New York
years.h: Fuse TV follows the world tour
years.p: NOFX's world tour is filmed for the series Backstage Passport. A second live album, recorded in San Francisco, follows on November 20.

eras.title: Old guitarists, a clown and a bad joke in Vegas
eras.text: The 25th anniversary brings two former guitarists back on stage. Four more albums follow, plus a memoir and a strange solo act for Fat Mike.

years.cap: NOFX on the steps of Leeds City Museum before the Leeds Academy show, April 29, 2009
years.h: Two former guitarists come back for the 25th anniversary
years.p: Steve Kidwiller and Dave Casillas play San Diego, Hollywood and San Francisco with NOFX.

years.h: Coaster comes out with Bill Stevenson co-producing
years.p: The eleventh album lands April 28. The Cokie the Clown EP follows in November.

years.cap: Fat Mike on bass, blue hair
years.h: Cokie the Clown gets Fat Mike banned from Emo's
years.p: Fat Mike plays SXSW in Austin as Cokie the Clown. A stunt involving urine gets him banned from the club.
years.xp: Wikipedia calls the SXSW set strange, emotional and intimate. A video showed Fat Mike urinating into a Patron bottle, then swapping in a clean one before the performance, and suggested audience members unknowingly drank it.

years.cap: El Hefe on trumpet at The Observatory, Santa Ana, California, December 14, 2012
years.h: Self Entitled arrives after a Canadian run
years.p: The twelfth studio album follows the 2011 Great White North tour of Canada and comes ahead of a 30th anniversary vinyl box set.

years.h: The band's autobiography is called The Hepatitis Bathtub
years.p: NOFX: The Hepatitis Bathtub and Other Stories, written with Jeff Alulis, comes out April 17.
years.xp: A special hardcover edition came with a vinyl record and a towel.

years.h: "Six Years on Dope" gets there before the album
years.p: First Ditch Effort, NOFX's thirteenth studio album, follows on October 7.

years.h: A Vegas joke costs NOFX a sponsor and a festival slot
years.p: After jokes about the 2017 Las Vegas shooting at a show there, Stone Brewing drops the band from its Punk in Drublic festival. The band apologizes.
years.xp:
Eric Melvin's line on stage, per Wikipedia: "I guess you only get shot in Vegas if you're in a country band." The band later said: "What we said in Vegas was shitty and insensitive."

NOFX and Me First and the Gimme Gimmes were removed from the Camp Punk in Drublic lineup.

eras.title: One last full lap
eras.text: Two late albums, a pandemic, and a farewell that turns three nights in San Pedro into a parade.

years.h: A single about mass shootings sends its money to Moms Demand Action
years.p: "Fish in a Gun Barrel" is the band's answer, with proceeds going to the gun-safety group.

years.h: Pandemic sessions for Single Album run tense
years.p: It's NOFX's fourteenth studio album. Spin's oral history has Fat Mike and Eric Melvin at odds over the band's direction while it was made.
years.xp:
Fat Mike called it "our best reviewed album ever," per Spin.

The same account has Fat Mike speaking about struggling with cocaine, opioids and alcohol, about three interventions, and about a 2021 hospitalization and rehab during the pandemic.

years.h: Fat Mike sets an end date for NOFX
years.p: The band will break up for its 40th anniversary. Per Spin's oral history, Erik Sandin finds out as a surprise.
years.xp: Sandin told Spin it was "like stumbling across your wife on Pornhub."

years.cap: Erik Sandin on drums at Rock im Park, Nuremberg
years.h: Double Album closes the discography
years.p: It is NOFX's fifteenth and final studio album.

years.cap: Fat Mike at Rock im Park, Nuremberg
q: We've become one of those legacy bands.
yt: The last song played live, "The Decline"
years.h: Three last nights at home in San Pedro
years.p: NOFX plays its final shows on October 4, 5 and 6, after 41 years. Spin puts the crowd at about 15,000.
years.xp: NOFX premiered a new song, "We Did It Our Way", on the last night, described by Fat Mike as his thank-you to fans. Farewell-tour crowds ran far bigger than the usual 2,000 to 3,000, per Spin.

sources.title: Spin: NOFX's final days in their own words
